_comment: The answer key. Each entry names a question, the context asking it, and the
document that should come back. `rationale` says what the question is for: without
it a later reader cannot tell a boundary probe from a baseline, and the set rots.
`expected_section` is not scored. It is there so a failure tells you whether the
right document came back on the wrong chunk, which is the first thing you want to
know. An empty `expected_doc_keys` means the correct answer is no results at all.
`forbidden_doc_keys` names documents that must NOT come back. An authorization
question needs this rather than an empty expectation: the asker may legitimately
see other documents that match loosely, so 'returned nothing' is the wrong bar and
'never returned this one' is the real rule. A forbidden document appearing is a
leak, not a ranking miss, and should be read that way.
The embedder is lexical (src/eval/embedding.py), so a question phrased with none of
its document's vocabulary will miss no matter how well chunking performs. Phrase
questions the way the documents do, and keep that limitation in mind when reading

questions.query: What is CPSIF?
questions.rationale: baseline: the document's own subject, stated in its opening

questions.query: When is CUCAI 2027?
questions.rationale: baseline: a date in the opening paragraph

questions.query: What is the project developer application deadline?
questions.rationale: baseline: a dated answer stated plainly in an early section

questions.query: Who do I email about CPSIF?
questions.rationale: baseline, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's own example query; the answer is at the very end of a long document and the document never uses the word 'email'

questions.query: What is the reimbursement limit for a single CPSIF claim?
questions.rationale: buried: a dollar figure after a long procedure, well past the opening

questions.query: What happens to unspent MLF budget at year end?
questions.rationale: buried: a late clause; CPSIF states the same rule, so the wrong fund is a live competitor

questions.query: Who approves an EigenAI compute request?
questions.rationale: buried in loosely structured prose with no headings to chunk on

questions.query: What are the steps to submit a CPSIF expense claim?
questions.rationale: boundary-straddling: a six-step numbered procedure long enough to split

questions.query: What are the eligibility requirements for MLF funding?
questions.rationale: boundary-straddling: a bulleted list plus the qualifying paragraph after it

questions.query: What is the CPSIF travel reimbursement limit per person?
questions.rationale: boundary-straddling: a short section between two longer ones, easily absorbed

questions.query: MLF
questions.rationale: bare acronym: exercises the keyword branch; CPSIF's guide also names MLF

questions.query: project developer technical assessment
questions.rationale: exact term: a role name plus a section term, no sentence around it; the term also appears in Timeline and How to apply, so the right chunk is not the only candidate

questions.query: AI² sponsorship tiers
questions.rationale: competitor: ARCHITECTURE.md flags AI² / GenAI Genesis / Academic Journal Workshops as events that blur together; CUCAI's document also mentions sponsorship

questions.query: When are AI² agent submissions due?
questions.rationale: baseline: a deadline stated in the opening section of a long document; the sponsorship package names the same event but holds no deadline

questions.query: What is the parameter cap for a submitted AI² agent?
questions.rationale: buried: a figure in a bulleted list deep inside a 7,600-character document, after two schedule tables

questions.query: What happens on the AI² finals day?
questions.rationale: boundary-straddling: a schedule table of ten rows plus the paragraph introducing it, split across chunks at smaller sizes

questions.query: What is the CUCAI registration fee?
questions.rationale: competitor: three documents carry dollar figures, only one states this fee

questions.query: Who is the EigenAI project lead?
questions.rationale: competitor: several documents name a lead; ranking, not presence, is the test

questions.query: What is the 2026-2027 departmental budget?
questions.rationale: authorization: alice holds the person grant and must see this

questions.query: What is the 2026-2027 departmental budget?
questions.rationale: authorization: the same question in a channel. A person grant must never reach a channel, so the transition report is forbidden. The channel can legitimately see other team-granted documents, which is why this is a forbidden-document question and not an expect-nothing one

questions.query: What is the parking policy at Bahen?
questions.rationale: expected-empty: plausible and genuinely absent; a set that only rewards finding things scores a system that returns everything as perfect
